artifacts.summary: 5-phase, 6.5-hour linear plan adding scripts/sapience-publish.sh with four write-surface subcommands (doc-comment, doc-version, dm, ko) plus a new test suite; widens file_scope by manifest.json (gate-3 provides.scripts parity is commit-blocking) and test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh (Case 30 lockstep array), and defers the single redeploy to the final phase so gate 3's deployed-vs-source drift rule never reopens mid-plan.

memory_candidates.content: Adding a new script to a Claude-Code extension's source store couples three gate-3 rules in check-extension-docs.sh that together dictate phase sequencing. (1) Rule at ~line 616 enumerates tracked files under <ext>/scripts/ via `git ls-files` and FAILs 'script file on disk NOT in provides.scripts' for any entry absent from manifest.json provides.scripts -- so the manifest edit must land in the SAME phase that creates the script, and the repair command the gate itself prints is `bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write`. (2) check_manifest_entries FAILs the reverse ('manifest script entry missing on disk'), so the manifest entry must never precede the file. (3) check_deployed_script_drift (~line 258) FAILs when a provides.scripts entry's deployed .claude/scripts/ copy differs from source, but explicitly SKIPS (info, never FAIL) when the deployed copy is ABSENT -- so registering pre-deploy is safe, while deploying mid-plan makes every later source edit a drift FAIL. The single redeploy therefore belongs after the last source edit, never earlier.

suite_selection_select's __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel is ABSORBING across a multi-path set: selecting over {a mapped path, an unmapped path} returns the bare sentinel, not the union of the mapped path's suites plus a sentinel. A plan phase that creates any new file therefore measures as __FULL_SWEEP__ over its whole Files-to-modify set regardless of how well its other paths map, and validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification check (which extracts any `test-*.sh` token from the justification block as a suitelist claim, then compares against the selector's actual output) will flag a naming-real-suites justification as a 'fabricated claim'. The honest authoring move for such a phase is the explicit sentinel claim plus naming verify-touched.sh (whose OWED-NOT-PAID fallback covers the unmapped paths) as the covering check -- and mentioning any test filename anywhere in the justification block, even as a command argument, flips the claim kind to suitelist.
